questions.subject: Computer Science and Information Technology
questions.text: Consider a processor that has [latex]16[/latex] general purpose registers and it uses [latex]2[/latex]-byte instruction format for all its instructions. Variable-sized opcodes are permitted. There are three different types of instructions; M-type, R-type, and C-type. Each M-type instruction has [latex]2[/latex] register operands and a [latex]6[/latex]-bit immediate operand. Each Rtype instruction has [latex]3[/latex] register operands. Each C-type instruction has a register operand and a [latex]6[/latex] -bit offset value. If there are [latex]2[/latex] unique M-type opcodes and [latex]7[/latex] unique R-type opcodes, which one of the following options gives the maximum number of unique opcodes possible for C-type instructions?

questions.subject: Computer Science and Information Technology
questions.text: Consider a binary search tree (BST) with [latex]n[/latex] leaf nodes [latex](n>0)[/latex]. Given any node [latex]V[/latex], the key present in the node is denoted as [latex]{Val}(V)[/latex]. All the keys present in the given BST are distinct. The keys belong to the set of real numbers. For a node [latex]V[/latex], let [latex]{Suc}(V)[/latex] denote the node that is its inorder successor. If a node [latex]V[/latex] does not have an inorder successor, then [latex]\operatorname{Suc}(V)[/latex] is [latex]N U L L[/latex]. As there are no duplicates, if [latex]{Suc}(V)[/latex] is not [latex]N U L L[/latex], then [latex]{Val}(V) < {Val}({Suc}(V))[/latex]. Corresponding to every leaf node [latex]L_{i}[/latex] that has a non-NULL [latex]\operatorname{Suc}\left(L_{i}\right)[/latex], a new key [latex]k_{i}[/latex] with the following property is to be inserted into the BST. [latex] {Val}\left(L_{i}\right) < k_{i} < Val ({Suc}(L_{i}))[/latex] Let [latex]K[/latex] represent the list of all such new keys to be inserted into the BST. Which of the following statements is/are true?

questions.subject: Computer Science and Information Technology
questions.text: Consider a stack [latex]S[/latex] and a queue [latex]Q[/latex]. Both of them are initially empty and have the capacity to store ten elements each. The elements [latex]1,2,3,4[/latex], and [latex]5[/latex] arrive one by one, in that order. When an element arrives, it is assigned either to [latex]S[/latex] (pushed on [latex]S[/latex] ) or to [latex]Q[/latex] (enqueued to [latex]Q[/latex] ). Once all the five elements are stored, the output is generated in two steps. First, stack S is emptied by popping all elements. Then queue [latex]Q[/latex] is emptied by dequeueing all elements. The output obtained by following this process is [latex]\text{4 3 1 2 5}[/latex]. Given the output, the objective is to predict whether an element was assigned to [latex]S[/latex] or [latex]Q[/latex]. Which of the following options is/are possible valid assignment(s) of the elements? Note: In the options, the notation [latex]x S[/latex] denotes that element [latex]x[/latex] was assigned to [latex]S[/latex] and [latex]y Q[/latex] denotes that element [latex]y[/latex] was assigned to [latex]Q[/latex].

Four words [latex]{P}, {Q}, {R}[/latex], and S are accessed by the processor in the same order [latex]10[/latex] times. That is, there are a total of [latex]40[/latex] memory references in the sequence [latex]{P}, {Q}, {R}, {S}, {P}, {Q}, {R}, {S}, \ldots[/latex] Assume that the cache memory is initially empty. The physical addresses of the words are given below ([latex]1[/latex] word [latex]=1[/latex] byte). [latex]\text{P: 0x845B32, Q: 0x845B26, R: 0x845B36, S: 0x846B32}[/latex] Which of the following statements is/are true? Note: [latex]1 {~K}=2^{10}[/latex] and [latex]1 {M}=2^{20}[/latex]

questions.subject: Computer Science and Information Technology
questions.text: To keep track of free blocks in a file system, one of the two approaches is generally used - using bitmaps (bit vectors) or using linked lists. Consider that the linked list approach is used to keep track of free blocks in a file system. Assume that the disk size is [latex]16[/latex] GB , block size is [latex]2[/latex] KB , and block numbers used are [latex]32[/latex]-bit long. A single pointer of size [latex]4[/latex] bytes is used in each block of the list to point to the next block of the list. The number of blocks required to hold the free disk block numbers is ________. (answer in integer) Note: [latex]1 {K}=2^{10}[/latex] and [latex]1 {G}=2^{30}[/latex]

questions.text: A system has a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) that has a reach of [latex]1[/latex] MB. TLB reach is defined as the total amount of physical memory that can be accessed through the TLB entries. The paging system uses pages of size [latex]4[/latex] KB. The virtual address space is [latex]64[/latex] GB and physical address space is [latex]1[/latex] GB. If each TLB entry stores a [latex]4[/latex]-bit process id, page number, frame number, and a [latex]2[/latex]-bit control field, then the size of the TLB (in bytes) is ________. questions.text: Consider contiguous allocation of physical memory to processes using variable partitioning scheme. questions.text: A non-pipelined instruction execution unit that operates at [latex]1.6[/latex] GHz clock takes an average of [latex]5[/latex] clock cycles to complete the execution of an instruction. To improve the performance, the system was pipelined with a goal of achieving an average throughput of one instruction per clock cycle. However, it could operate only at [latex]1.2[/latex] GHz due to pipeline overheads. While executing a program in the pipelined design, [latex]30 \%[/latex] of instructions encountered a stall of [latex]2[/latex] cycles due to pipeline hazards. The speed-up obtained by the pipelined design over the non-pipelined one for this program is ________(rounded off to two decimal places) Note: [latex]1 {G}=10^{9}[/latex]
